Buttons

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/custom-buttons.Rmd
custom-buttons.Rmd

Methods

The method of a go_updatemenu_button() determines which plotly.js function will be used to modify the chart. There are 4 possible methods:

  • "restyle": modify data or data attributes
  • "relayout": modify layout attributes
  • "update": modify data and layout attributes
  • "animate": start or pause an animation (see Animations)

Restyle Buttons

The "restyle" method should be used when modifying the data and data attributes of the graph
Update One Data Attribute This example demostrates how to update a single data attribute: line color with the "restyle" method.

library(plotly.core)

x <- seq(-2 * pi, 2 * pi, length.out = 1000)
df <- data.frame(x, y1 = sin(x))

df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = ~x, y = ~y1, mode = "lines") |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Button Restyle",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(domain = c(0.1, 1)),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "y"),
    updatemenus = list(
      go_updatemenu(
        type = "buttons",
        y = 0.8,
        buttons = list(
          go_updatemenu_button(
            method = "restyle",
            args = list("line.color", "blue"),
            label = "Blue"
          ),
          go_updatemenu_button(
            method = "restyle",
            args = list("line.color", "red"),
            label = "Red"
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )

Update Several Data Attributes This example demostrates how to update several data attributes: colorscale, chart type, and colorscale with the “restyle” method.

library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_heatmap(z = volcano, colorscale = "Rainbow")

restyle_button <- function(attr, value, label) {
  go_updatemenu_button(method = "restyle", args = list(attr, value), label = label)
}

# chart option buttons
chart_types <- go_updatemenu(
  type = "buttons",
  direction = "right",
  xanchor = "center",
  yanchor = "top",
  pad = go_updatemenu_pad(r = 0, t = 10, b = 10),
  x = 0.5,
  y = 1.27,
  buttons = list(
    restyle_button("type", "heatmap", "Heatmap"),
    restyle_button("type", "contour", "Contour"),
    restyle_button("type", "surface", "Surface")
  )
)

# color option buttons
color_types <- go_updatemenu(
  type = "buttons",
  direction = "right",
  xanchor = "center",
  yanchor = "top",
  pad = go_updatemenu_pad(r = 0, t = 10, b = 10),
  x = 0.5,
  y = 1.17,
  buttons = list(
    restyle_button("colorscale", "Rainbow", "Rainbow"),
    restyle_button("colorscale", "Jet", "Jet"),
    restyle_button("colorscale", "Earth", "Earth"),
    restyle_button("colorscale", "Electric", "Electric")
  )
)

annot <- list(
  go_annotation(
    text = "Chart<br>Type",
    x = 0.2,
    y = 1.25,
    xref = "paper",
    yref = "paper",
    showarrow = FALSE
  ),
  go_annotation(
    text = "Color<br>Type",
    x = 0.2,
    y = 1.15,
    xref = "paper",
    yref = "paper",
    showarrow = FALSE
  )
)

# plot
fig <- fig |>
  update_layout(
    xaxis = go_xaxis(domain = c(0.1, 1)),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "y"),
    updatemenus = list(chart_types, color_types),
    annotations = annot
  )

fig

Relayout Button

The "relayout" method should be used when modiying the layout attributes of the graph.
Update One Layout Attribute This example demostrated how to update a layout attribute: shapes with the "relayout" method.

library(plotly.core)

x0 <- rnorm(400, mean = 2, sd = 0.4)
y0 <- rnorm(400, mean = 2, sd = 0.4)
x1 <- rnorm(400, mean = 3, sd = 0.6)
y1 <- rnorm(400, mean = 6, sd = 0.4)
x2 <- rnorm(400, mean = 4, sd = 0.2)
y2 <- rnorm(400, mean = 4, sd = 0.4)

# shapes components
cluster_shape <- function(x, y, color) {
  go_shape(
    type = "circle",
    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",
    x0 = min(x),
    y0 = min(y),
    x1 = max(x),
    y1 = max(y),
    opacity = 0.25,
    line = go_shape_line(color = color),
    fillcolor = color
  )
}
cluster0 <- cluster_shape(x0, y0, "#835AF1")
cluster1 <- cluster_shape(x1, y1, "#7FA6EE")
cluster2 <- cluster_shape(x2, y2, "#B8F7D4")

shapes_button <- function(label, shapes) {
  go_updatemenu_button(
    label = label,
    method = "relayout",
    args = list(list(shapes = shapes))
  )
}

# updatemenus component
updatemenus <- list(
  go_updatemenu(
    active = -1,
    type = "buttons",
    buttons = list(
      shapes_button("None", list()),
      shapes_button("Cluster 0", list(cluster0)),
      shapes_button("Cluster 1", list(cluster1)),
      shapes_button("Cluster 2", list(cluster2)),
      shapes_button("All", list(cluster0, cluster1, cluster2))
    )
  )
)

go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = x0,
    y = y0,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(color = "#835AF1")
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = x1,
    y = y1,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(color = "#7FA6EE")
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = x2,
    y = y2,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(color = "#B8F7D4")
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Highlight Clusters",
    showlegend = FALSE,
    updatemenus = updatemenus
  )

Update Button

The "update" method should be used when modifying the data and layout sections of the graph. This example demostrates how to update which traces are diplayed while simultaneously updating layout attributes such as the chart title and annotations.

library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv")
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)

high_annotations <- go_annotation(
  x = df$Date[df$AAPL.High == max(df$AAPL.High)][[1]],
  y = max(df$AAPL.High),
  xref = "x",
  yref = "y",
  text = paste0("High: $", max(df$AAPL.High)),
  ax = 0,
  ay = -40
)

low_annotations <- go_annotation(
  x = df$Date[df$AAPL.Low == min(df$AAPL.Low)][[1]],
  y = min(df$AAPL.Low),
  xref = "x",
  yref = "y",
  text = paste0("Low: $", min(df$AAPL.Low)),
  ax = 0,
  ay = 40
)

update_button <- function(label, visible, title, annotations) {
  go_updatemenu_button(
    label = label,
    method = "update",
    args = list(
      list(visible = visible),
      list(title = title, annotations = annotations)
    )
  )
}

# updatemenus component
updatemenus <- list(
  go_updatemenu(
    active = -1,
    type = "buttons",
    buttons = list(
      update_button("High", c(FALSE, TRUE), "Apple High", list(high_annotations)),
      update_button("Low", c(TRUE, FALSE), "Apple Low", list(low_annotations)),
      update_button(
        "Both",
        c(TRUE, TRUE),
        "Apple",
        list(low_annotations, high_annotations)
      ),
      update_button("Reset", c(TRUE, TRUE), "Apple", list())
    )
  )
)

df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~AAPL.High,
    name = "High",
    mode = "lines",
    line = go_scatter_line(color = "#33CFA5")
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~AAPL.Low,
    name = "Low",
    mode = "lines",
    line = go_scatter_line(color = "#F06A6A")
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Apple",
    showlegend = FALSE,
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "Date"),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Price ($)"),
    updatemenus = updatemenus
  )

Animate Button

See Animations for figures with play and pause buttons.

Style Buttons

When adding buttons to Plotly charts, users have the option of styling the color, font, padding, and position of the buttons. The example below demostrates hot to apply different styling options. See all updatemenus styling attributes in go_updatemenu().

Tile Maps

Tile maps (add_scattermap() and go_map()) are drawn with MapLibre and need no access token. See our Map Layers documentation for more information.

library(plotly.core)

# read in wind turbines data
df_wind <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.r-docs/master/r/data/2805.csv")

# subset and clean data
df_sub <- subset(df_wind, manufac != "unknown", select = c(lat_DD, long_DD, manufac))

# the largest wind farms (by number of turbines), at their median location
df_farms <- subset(df_wind, !grepl("^unknown", site_name))
df_farms <- aggregate(
  cbind(Latitude = lat_DD, Longitude = long_DD) ~ site_name,
  data = df_farms,
  FUN = median
)
turbines <- table(df_wind$site_name)
df_farms$turbines <- as.vector(turbines[df_farms$site_name])
df_farms <- df_farms[order(-df_farms$turbines), ]
df_farms$Wind.Farm <- df_farms$site_name
rm(df_wind)

# location buttons
usa <- go_updatemenu_button(
  method = "relayout",
  args = list(list(
    map.center.lat = median(df_sub$lat_DD),
    map.center.lon = median(df_sub$long_DD),
    map.zoom = 3
  )),
  label = "USA"
)

buttons <- function(i) {
  go_updatemenu_button(
    method = "relayout",
    args = list(list(
      map.center.lat = df_farms$Latitude[i],
      map.center.lon = df_farms$Longitude[i],
      map.zoom = 9
    )),
    label = df_farms$Wind.Farm[i]
  )
}

# map style buttons
style_button <- function(style, label) {
  go_updatemenu_button(
    method = "relayout",
    args = list(list(map.style = style)),
    label = label
  )
}
basic <- style_button("carto-voyager", "Basic")
dark <- style_button("carto-darkmatter", "Dark")
satellite <- style_button("satellite", "Satellite")

# plot one scattermap trace per manufacturer, with buttons
df_sub |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scattermap(
    lat = ~lat_DD,
    lon = ~long_DD,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scattermap_marker(size = 3),
    split = ~manufac
  ) |>
  add_annotation(
    x = 0.05,
    y = 0.05,
    text = "All US wind turbines (scroll to zoom)",
    xref = "paper",
    yref = "paper",
    showarrow = FALSE,
    font = go_font(color = "magenta", size = 14)
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    plot_bgcolor = "black",
    paper_bgcolor = "black",
    map = go_map(
      center = go_map_center(
        lat = median(df_sub$lat_DD),
        lon = median(df_sub$long_DD)
      ),
      zoom = 3,
      style = "carto-darkmatter"
    ),
    updatemenus = list(
      go_updatemenu(
        type = "buttons",
        direction = "right",
        xanchor = "center",
        yanchor = "top",
        pad = go_updatemenu_pad(r = 0, t = 10, b = 10),
        x = 0.5,
        y = 1,
        showactive = FALSE,
        buttons = list(usa, buttons(1), buttons(2), buttons(3), buttons(4))
      ),
      go_updatemenu(
        type = "buttons",
        direction = "right",
        xanchor = "center",
        yanchor = "top",
        pad = go_updatemenu_pad(r = 0, t = 10, b = 10),
        x = 0.5,
        y = 0.935,
        showactive = FALSE,
        buttons = list(buttons(6), buttons(7), buttons(8), buttons(9))
      ),
      go_updatemenu(
        type = "buttons",
        direction = "right",
        yanchor = "bottom",
        x = 1,
        y = 0,
        buttons = list(dark, basic, satellite)
      )
    )
  )
